description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries. Should-trigger covers DE + EN phrasings for worktree governance (scope lock, merge-readiness status, scoped verification, safe cleanup). Should-not-trigger covers the near-miss neighbours (plain branch switch, git-worktree info question, subagent-orchestration mode selection, worktree creation mechanics, remote branch deletion) whose vocabulary overlaps.

queries.q: declare a scope lock for this worktree before I start editing
is this worktree merge-ready? check dirty state, ahead/behind and verification evidence
clean up the finished worktrees but make sure no unmerged commits get lost
welche Worktrees sind noch aktiv, und welche Pfade gehören welchem Worktree?
run the scoped verification for the change in this worktree, not the full CI
switch to the feature branch and continue working there
queries.note: plain branch switch, no worktree governance → git-workflow

queries.q: what does the output of git worktree list mean?
queries.note: git info question, not lifecycle governance

queries.q: which subagent-orchestration mode should I pick for these three independent tasks?
queries.note: mode selection → subagent-orchestration; worktrees only enter after a mode is chosen

queries.q: spawn a worktree with ignore-safety checks and a clean test baseline for this refactor
delete the old release branch on origin
queries.note: remote branch deletion, no worktree involved → git-workflow (permission-gated)
